name: 1816 Prairie Avenue — Henderson Second Empire (district draft; refined by T-1886)

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 22.750, v 0.250 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the georeference's independent check is 1.47 m RMS. Rotation -0.621 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1816 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1816 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28).

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle that fits inside the traced main part (u toward the street, v along the front). The building's other rectangles are in draft_plan.

stories.note: '3S.B.; rear2B' printed on the 1911 sheet: 3 full storeys.

Storeys per piece and roof per piece are the draft rules' (reconstructed).

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row 'Second Empire' overlaid with the frontage row: Second Empire: the register's mansard with dormers over the mapped rounded front bays, which the fitted plan carries as a projecting bay. Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 715317729 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %. draft.note: The draft's own provenance: the pass that wrote it, the rows it read and the tickets that replace it attribute by attribute under this id.

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 28.
what_it_supplies: The water's edge beside the Illinois Central from about 40 m north of 18th Street to about 80 m south of it, and the easternmost track on to the paper's edge, as of 1911
The 1800 Prairie lot and the Glessner House footprint (stone, courtyard plan) as of 1911, and every Prairie- and Calumet-facing footprint from 18th to 20th Street
Its own printed Scale of Feet
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2329, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1886 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 28 trace (s28fp-1816-b1), the T-1841 census (s28-1816-front, s28-1816-wing) and the T-1837 register row frontage-28-039 (Henderson Second Empire); every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-prairie-18-20-west-2329).
